title: 16 November 1974. Humanity sent a message to the stars as part of a ceremony.
description:
Humanity sent a message to the stars as part of a ceremony. Arecibo broadcast it to mark the remodelling of its telescope. It was a demonstration of technology, not a serious attempt at conversation.

Frank Drake wrote it, with help. Carl Sagan and other colleagues contributed to the design.

The length of the message. It is 73 times 23, both prime, which hints at how to fold it into a picture.

Numbers, DNA, a stick figure and the telescope. It counts one to ten, gives the atomic numbers of five elements, shows DNA, a human 1.764 metres tall, a population of about four billion, the Solar System and the dish.

The whole thing took under three minutes. It went out at 10 bits a second.

One number was already out of date. The message gave a figure for human DNA base pairs that was believed correct in 1974. The count is now known to be about 3.2 billion.

It will take more than 20,000 years to arrive. The target is M13, a star cluster. The SETI Institute says it is unlikely to prompt a reply.

The most powerful broadcast we aimed at the stars was part of a ceremony.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arecibo_message: read. Established the 16 November 1974 date, that it was broadcast at a ceremony marking the remodelling of the telescope, that it was meant as a demonstration of human technological achievement rather than a real attempt at conversation, that it was 1,679 bits arranged 73 rows by 23 columns (a semiprime), that the broadcast lasted under three minutes, the contents (numbers 1 to 10, atomic numbers of hydrogen, carbon, nitrogen, oxygen and phosphorus, DNA, a human figure of 1.764 m, a population of about 4 billion, the Solar System, the dish), that the genome figure was believed correct in 1974 but is now known to be about 3.2 billion base pairs, and that the message will take at least 25,000 years to reach M13.
- https://www.seti.org/research/seti-101/project-phoenix/arecibo/: read. Established the 1974 broadcast as part of ceremonies for a major upgrade, 1,679 bits as 73 lines of 23 characters, a broadcast under three minutes at 10 bits per second, the target M13, and the statement that it is unlikely the short inquiry will prompt a reply.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Drake: read. Established that Drake designed and wrote the Arecibo message in 1974.
